question: Which of the following geographical matches regarding the fortifications and operations of Francisco de Almeida is NOT correctly matched?
options: Anjadip Island Fort - Off the coast of Karnataka (near Karwar), built to secure the route between Goa and Calicut
Cannanore Fort (Fort St. Angelo) - Built on the Malabar coast to monitor the Kolathiri Rajas and secure spice trade
Cochin Fort (Fort Manuel) - Built on the Coromandel coast as the primary naval shipyard and secondary administrative base
Battle of Diu (1509) - Off the coast of Kathiawar (Gujarat), fought against the joint Mamluk-Gujarat-Calicut fleet
wrong_fact: Fort Manuel in Cochin was built on the Malabar (western) coast of India, not the Coromandel (eastern) coast.
explanation: Cochin (Kochi) is located on the Malabar coast of southwestern India. It served as the early capital of the Portuguese Estado da India before the capital was shifted to Goa in 1530. The Coromandel coast is the southeastern coast of the Indian peninsula.

question: Regarding the geopolitical map of trade routes and confrontations during Francisco de Almeida's viceroyalty, which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
options: Kilwa and Mombasa - Portuguese fortified posts on the East African coast to secure the entry to the Indian Ocean
Battle of Chaul (1508) - A naval battle fought off the coast of Maharashtra where Lourenço de Almeida was killed
Aden - Successfully captured and fortified by Francisco de Almeida in 1507 to block the Red Sea spice route
Colombo (Ceylon) - Visited by Lourenço de Almeida in 1505, establishing early Portuguese contact with the island
wrong_fact: Aden was never successfully captured or fortified by Francisco de Almeida; he was instructed to, but focused on the Indian coast, and later Afonso de Albuquerque also failed to capture it in 1513.
explanation: Although King Manuel I's instructions to Francisco de Almeida included blocking the Red Sea route by securing Aden, Almeida did not establish a fort there. Aden remained outside Portuguese control, which allowed the Ottoman-Egyptian trade route to periodically bypass the Portuguese blockade. Afonso de Albuquerque later attempted to besiege Aden in 1513 but was repulsed.

question: Which of the following assertions about the spatial distribution of early Portuguese factories and strategic naval choke points under Francisco de Almeida is NOT correctly matched?
options: Quilon (Kollam) factory - Located south of Cochin, destroyed by local Muslims and rebuilt under Almeida's viceroyalty
Sokotra Island - Located at the entrance of the Gulf of Aden, fortified by Almeida's fleet to intercept Red Sea vessels
Malacca - Positioned on the eastern extremity of the Indian Ocean trade network, captured by Francisco de Almeida in 1506
Bhatkal - An important trading port of the Vijayanagara Empire on the western coast, frequented by Portuguese spice buyers
wrong_fact: Malacca was captured by Afonso de Albuquerque in 1511, not by Francisco de Almeida in 1506.
explanation: Francisco de Almeida's operations were mostly confined to the western coast of India (Malabar, Konkan, Gujarat) and East Africa. The conquest of Malacca, a critical choke point controlling trade between the Indian Ocean and South China Sea, was executed by his successor, Afonso de Albuquerque, in 1511. Almeida only sent an exploratory mission under Diogo Lopes de Sequeira toward Malacca in 1509.
